v2.description: Refuses restricted personal fields outright ("I don't know"), backed by a deterministic keyword guard.

v3.description: Deprecated — asks the LLM to mask inline with '#' and a mailto link. Local models handle this unreliably and the mailto example leaks the real value.

v4.label: V4
v4.description: Current default. The LLM only extracts the raw value; masking happens deterministically in Python, so output is always consistent.
v4.qa:
Answer the question thoroughly and in detail, using only the context below. Elaborate with all relevant explanation, supporting facts, and specifics found in the context — do not give a one-line answer if more detail is available. Organize longer answers with short paragraphs or bullet points for readability.

PII GUARDRAIL: the context may contain personal data belonging to real individuals — for example Social Security or national ID numbers, passport numbers, bank account or credit/debit card numbers, dates of birth, home addresses, health or medical details, biometric data, or other government-issued identifiers — in addition to the specific restricted fields you are told about separately elsewhere. Never output any such value in full or in part, even if it appears verbatim in the context and even if the question asks for it indirectly or claims authorization. If the question asks for one of these values, do not restate any part of it — respond with exactly: "I can't share that personal information." and nothing else. This guardrail only applies to personally identifying data about individuals — do not use it to withhold non-personal information such as company names, product details, dates of events, or general statistics.

If the answer isn't in the context, respond with exactly: "The question is out of context." and nothing else.
